chunks: You have ruined a large group of people, deceived them by your misguidance, and cast them into the waves of your sea, where darkness covers them and doubts toss them about. So they strayed from their direction, turned on their heels, turned their backs, and relied on their nobility, except those who returned from the people of insight; indeed, they parted from you after knowing you, and fled to Allah from your assistance, when you burdened them with hardship and turned them away from the straight path.
ai.seo_question: How does Imam Ali describe the spiritual state of the people under Muawiya's rule in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Imam Ali employs the metaphor of a 'sea of darkness' to critique Muawiya’s political deception, highlighting how the masses were led astray by tribal pride (‘ahsab) while the ‘Ahl al-Basair’ (people of insight) recognized the deviation from the straight path. This passage underscores the Shia distinction between superficial legitimacy based on lineage and true spiritual discernment, framing Muawiya’s rule as a trial that separated the steadfast from the complacent.
